summary.en: How two things move together, why that isn't proof, and how to look ahead.
summary.bs: Kako se dvije stvari kreću zajedno, zašto to nije dokaz i kako gledati unaprijed.

en.one: Correlation measures how closely two variables move together, from −1 to +1.
en.explain: +1 means they rise together perfectly, −1 means one falls exactly as the other rises, and 0 means no straight-line relationship. In real business data, 0.3 is weak, 0.5 moderate, and above 0.7 strong.
en.example: Across 50 days, ice-cream sales and temperature have a correlation of 0.8: hot days, high sales.
en.why: It helps you spot which factors are worth a closer look, like what moves your sales.
en.mixup: A correlation of 0 doesn't mean no relationship at all. It only means no straight-line one; a curve can hide.

bs.one: Correlation (korelacija) mjeri koliko se dvije varijable kreću zajedno, od −1 do +1.
bs.explain: +1 znači da savršeno rastu zajedno, −1 da jedna pada tačno koliko druga raste, a 0 da nema linearne veze. U stvarnim poslovnim podacima 0,3 je slaba, 0,5 umjerena, a iznad 0,7 jaka.
bs.example: Kroz 50 dana, prodaja sladoleda i temperatura imaju korelaciju 0,8: vrući dani, visoka prodaja.
bs.why: Pomaže ti da primijetiš koji faktori zaslužuju bliži pogled, npr. šta pokreće prodaju.
bs.mixup: Korelacija 0 ne znači da nema nikakve veze. Znači samo da nema linearne; kriva može biti skrivena.

en.one: Two things moving together doesn't prove that one causes the other.
en.explain: A third factor may drive both, the cause might run the other way, or it may be coincidence. The way to test cause is an experiment: change one thing on purpose for a random group, keep everything else the same, and compare.
en.example: Stores with more staff have higher sales. But busy locations get more staff because they're busy; adding staff to a quiet store won't create customers.
en.why: Mistaking correlation for cause leads to expensive actions that don't work.
en.mixup: 'The data shows X causes Y' is a red flag unless there was an experiment or very careful analysis.

bs.one: Kad se dvije stvari kreću zajedno, to ne dokazuje da jedna uzrokuje drugu.
bs.explain: Treći faktor može pokretati obje, uzrok može ići obrnuto ili je slučajnost. Uzrok se testira eksperimentom: namjerno promijeni jednu stvar za slučajnu grupu, sve ostalo drži isto i uporedi.
bs.example: Radnje s više osoblja imaju veću prodaju. Ali prometne lokacije dobiju više osoblja jer su prometne; dodavanje osoblja u mirnu radnju neće stvoriti kupce.
bs.why: Miješanje korelacije s uzrokom vodi do skupih poteza koji ne rade.
bs.mixup: 'Podaci pokazuju da X uzrokuje Y' je crvena zastavica, osim ako je bio eksperiment ili vrlo pažljiva analiza.

en.one: Regression finds the line that best fits your data, so you can describe and predict how one variable changes with another.
en.explain: Simple linear regression draws a straight trend line through a scatter plot. Its slope tells you how much Y changes for each 1-unit change in X. Spreadsheets add it in one click ('Add trendline').
en.example: Regression on past data shows that each extra €100 of ads came with about €450 more sales, within the range you've tried.
en.why: It turns a cloud of dots into a usable rule of thumb for planning.
en.mixup: A trend line isn't valid forever. Outside the range of your data, like 10 times more ad spend, the relationship can break down.

bs.one: Regression (regresija) nalazi liniju koja najbolje odgovara podacima, da možeš opisati i predvidjeti kako se jedna varijabla mijenja s drugom.
bs.explain: Jednostavna linearna regresija povuče pravu liniju trenda kroz dijagram raspršenosti. Njen nagib govori koliko se Y promijeni za svaku promjenu X za 1 jedinicu. Tabele je dodaju jednim klikom ('Add trendline').
bs.example: Regresija na prošlim podacima pokaže da je svakih dodatnih 100 € reklama išlo uz oko 450 € više prodaje, unutar raspona koji si probao.
bs.why: Pretvara oblak tačaka u upotrebljivo pravilo za planiranje.
bs.mixup: Linija trenda ne važi zauvijek. Izvan raspona tvojih podataka, npr. 10 puta veći budžet za reklame, veza se može slomiti.

en.one: Seasonality is a pattern that repeats at the same time every year, month, week or day.
en.explain: Tourism peaks in summer, gift shops in December, cafés at 8 am, restaurants on Fridays. When you compare numbers, compare with the same period last year ('year over year'), not with last month, or the season fools you.
en.example: A seaside shop's sales drop 60% from August to October. That's not a crisis; the same drop happened every year.
en.why: Knowing your seasons lets you plan stock, staff and cash for the quiet months.
en.mixup: A seasonal rise is not growth. Growth is when this summer beats last summer.

bs.one: Seasonality (sezonalnost) je obrazac koji se ponavlja u isto vrijeme svake godine, mjeseca, sedmice ili dana.
bs.explain: Turizam je na vrhuncu ljeti, radnje s poklonima u decembru, kafići u 8 ujutro, restorani petkom. Kad porediš brojeve, poredi s istim periodom prošle godine ('godina na godinu'), a ne s prošlim mjesecom, inače te sezona prevari.
bs.example: Prodaja radnje na moru padne 60% od augusta do oktobra. To nije kriza; isti pad se desio svake godine.
bs.why: Kad znaš svoje sezone, planiraš zalihe, ljude i novac za mirne mjesece.
bs.mixup: Sezonski rast nije rast. Rast je kad ovo ljeto pobijedi prošlo ljeto.

en.one: A moving average smooths out daily ups and downs by averaging the last few periods, updated as each new period arrives.
en.explain: A 7-day moving average of sales takes today and the 6 days before, then shifts forward by one day. It hides random noise and weekday patterns, so the real trend is easier to see.
en.example: Daily sales jump around between €600 and €1,400, but the 7-day moving average shows a steady climb from €850 to €950 over the month.
en.why: It helps you react to real changes, not to one good or bad day.
en.mixup: A moving average always lags. It shows a turning point a few days after it actually happened.

bs.one: Moving average (pokretni prosjek) izravnava dnevne uspone i padove uprosječivanjem zadnjih nekoliko perioda, a ažurira se sa svakim novim periodom.
bs.explain: 7-dnevni pokretni prosjek prodaje uzme danas i 6 dana prije, pa se pomjeri za jedan dan. Sakrije slučajni šum i obrasce dana u sedmici, pa je stvarni trend lakše vidjeti.
bs.example: Dnevna prodaja skače između 600 € i 1.400 €, ali 7-dnevni pokretni prosjek pokazuje stalan rast s 850 € na 950 € tokom mjeseca.
bs.why: Pomaže ti da reaguješ na stvarne promjene, a ne na jedan dobar ili loš dan.
bs.mixup: Pokretni prosjek uvijek kasni. Pokaže preokret par dana nakon što se stvarno desio.

en.one: Forecasting is using past data and known plans to estimate future numbers like sales, costs or demand.
en.explain: Simple methods work well: last year's same month plus your recent growth rate, adjusted for known events. Always give a range (best, expected, worst) instead of one exact number, and compare forecasts with what actually happened to learn.
en.example: Last December's sales were €30,000 and the business is growing about 10% a year, so this December's forecast is about €33,000, with a range of €29,000–€36,000.
en.why: Forecasts drive orders, hiring and cash planning; a reasonable forecast beats none.
en.mixup: A forecast is not a target or a promise. Mixing the two makes people bend the numbers.

bs.one: Forecasting (prognoziranje) je korištenje prošlih podataka i poznatih planova za procjenu budućih brojeva kao što su prodaja, troškovi ili potražnja.
bs.explain: Jednostavne metode dobro rade: isti mjesec prošle godine plus nedavna stopa rasta, prilagođeno za poznate događaje. Uvijek daj raspon (najbolje, očekivano, najgore) umjesto jednog tačnog broja i poredi prognoze sa stvarnim rezultatima da učiš.
bs.example: Prošlog decembra prodaja je bila 30.000 €, a posao raste oko 10% godišnje, pa je prognoza za ovaj decembar oko 33.000 €, s rasponom 29.000–36.000 €.
bs.why: Prognoze pokreću narudžbe, zapošljavanje i planiranje novca; razumna prognoza je bolja nego nikakva.
bs.mixup: Prognoza nije cilj ni obećanje. Kad se to dvoje pomiješa, ljudi naštimavaju brojeve.

q.en: Stores with more staff sell more. Should you add staff to a quiet store to boost sales?
q.bs: Radnje s više osoblja više prodaju. Treba li dodati osoblje u mirnu radnju da poveća prodaju?

options.en: Not on this evidence; busy stores get more staff because they're busy
options.bs: Ne na osnovu ovoga; prometne radnje dobiju više osoblja jer su prometne

explain.en: Correlation isn't causation; here the cause likely runs the other way.
explain.bs: Korelacija nije uzročnost; ovdje uzrok vjerovatno ide obrnuto.

q.en: Sales fell 60% from August to October, as they do every year. This is…
q.bs: Prodaja je pala 60% od augusta do oktobra, kao svake godine. To je…

explain.en: A pattern that repeats each year is seasonality; compare year over year.
explain.bs: Obrazac koji se ponavlja svake godine je sezonalnost; poredi godinu na godinu.

q.en: Last December: €30,000. Growth: about 10% a year. What's a sensible forecast for this December?
q.bs: Prošli decembar: 30.000 €. Rast: oko 10% godišnje. Koja je razumna prognoza za ovaj decembar?

q.en: A correlation of −0.8 between price and units sold means…
q.bs: Korelacija od −0,8 između cijene i prodanih komada znači…

options.en: Higher prices go with clearly fewer sales
options.bs: Više cijene idu uz jasno manju prodaju

explain.en: Negative and strong: as one goes up, the other tends to go down.
explain.bs: Negativna i jaka: kad jedna raste, druga obično pada.
